chunks.heading: Test Centers
chunks.text:
Test Centers
KUCAT-CBT 2026 is conducted at five centers: Lalitpur, Dhulikhel, Biratnagar, Butwal, and Pokhara. The test is computer-based and is not available online — it must be taken in person at one of these centers.

chunks.heading: Test Format Overview
chunks.text:
Test Format Overview
The KUCAT-CBT lasts two hours in total and contains 120 multiple-choice questions. The test is split into three parts — one for each subject in the candidate's chosen stream (PCM or PCB) — with 40 questions per part. Each subject's syllabus has 40 topics, and exactly one question is asked per topic. Candidates cannot skip a question or return to one already submitted, but they can freely switch between the three subject parts at any time during the test. Scores are shown to the candidate at the end of the test.

chunks.heading: Adaptive Difficulty and Scoring
chunks.text:
Adaptive Difficulty and Scoring
Each part of the test starts with a difficulty level 1 question. Answering a question correctly raises the difficulty of the next question by one level; answering incorrectly lowers it by one level. Difficulty level 5 (the hardest) doesn't increase further after a correct answer, and difficulty level 1 (the easiest) doesn't decrease further after an incorrect answer.

Each correct answer adds points based on the question's difficulty level:
 
- Level 1: 11 points
- Level 2: 13 points
- Level 3: 15 points
- Level 4: 17 points
- Level 5: 19 points
A candidate's score starts at zero, and total CBT scores range from 0 to 2220.

chunks.heading: Exam Day Rules and Procedure
chunks.text:
Exam Day Rules and Procedure
Candidates must arrive at least 30 minutes before their test's scheduled start time. Arriving late shortens the candidate's available time — the two-hour limit is not extended for latecomers for any reason. Candidates must bring their color-printed admission card and the original identification document used during application; scanned copies, printouts, or photos of the ID are not accepted as valid originals.
 
Personal calculators are not allowed; a calculator is available on the test computer if needed. Only pens and pencils may be brought into the test room — no other electronic devices or writing materials are permitted, and mobile phones and wireless devices are strictly prohibited.

Once seated, candidates log in with credentials provided after ID verification, confirm their name on screen, and choose which of the three subjects to start with — the timer begins as soon as a subject is selected. Candidates having difficulty during the test should raise their hand to call an invigilator, and may not communicate with or look at other candidates' screens. Restroom breaks are only allowed starting 30 minutes after the test begins, and must be completed at least 15 minutes before the test's end time.

chunks.heading: One Application, One Attempt Rule
chunks.text:
One Application, One Attempt Rule
Each candidate may submit only one application and take the KUCAT-CBT only once. If a candidate is found to have submitted multiple applications, or appears for the test more than once, all of their exam attempts are cancelled and they are disqualified from the admission process.
